rules.name: Questionnaire flow
rules.statement: The questionnaire has exactly eight steps in this order (assumption D-047). Each question appears only when at least one receiving party needs the answer for this person. Answers are saved as the employee goes; the employee can resume until submitting; going back and changing an earlier answer keeps the other answers until submission; submitting needs one confirmation on a summary page (D-050). For Liechtenstein residents the cross-border questions come before the source tax details, which are skipped when there is in principle no source tax liability (D-040).

table.then: First name, last name, date of birth, first working day - asked of everyone.
Street, house number (or 'no house number'), postcode, town, country as on the first working day - everyone; canton only if living in Switzerland.
Only employees living in Switzerland: nationality; C permit (yes/no) only if not Swiss.
Civil status for everyone; spouse's date of birth if Married, Registered partnership or Separated; spouse's nationality, C permit and residence in Switzerland only for spouse exemption check.
Only residents of Liechtenstein or Germany (all subject to source tax): the daily-return and non-return-day questions, and for Germany the certificate of residence.
Only employees subject to source tax (and not exempt in principle as Liechtenstein residents): denomination, spouse gainfully employed (married/registered partners), has children.
Only if the employee has children: one block per child with the child questions.
Permit reminder (non-Swiss or living abroad), summary page, one confirmation to submit.

rules.name: Insurance start date
rules.statement: The pension fund insurance start date is derived from the first working day (the contractual start date, assumption D-039), never asked: if the first working day is the 1st of a month, insurance starts that day; otherwise on the 1st of the following month (e.g. 15.03.2026 gives 01.04.2026). It is always derived again from the latest first working day.
inputs: First working day is the 1st of a month

table.then: Insurance starts on the first working day.
Insurance starts on the 1st of the following month.

rules.name: Civil status for the pension fund
rules.statement: The fund only accepts Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed. Registered partnership and Separated are entered as Married (with the partner's/spouse's date of birth); the others unchanged (assumption D-003).

rules.name: Canton for the pension fund
rules.statement: Employees living in Switzerland: the canton they chose. Employees living abroad: the canton of the place of work, Zurich for Muster AG, not asked (assumption D-002).

rules.name: Subject to source tax
rules.statement: An employee living abroad is subject to source tax whatever their nationality. An employee living in Switzerland is subject only if not Swiss (Swiss citizenship, also as dual nationality, counts as Swiss), without a C permit, and not married or in a registered partnership with a Swiss national or C-permit holder who lives in Switzerland. Separated counts as single, so no spouse exemption. ('Here' in HR's wording means Switzerland; assumption D-043.) Always derived again from the latest answers.
rules.expression: address_country != null and (address_country != "Switzerland" or (nationality != "Switzerland" and holds_c_permit == "no" and not (civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"] and (spouse_nationality == "Switzerland" or spouse_holds_c_permit == "yes") and spouse_residence_country == "yes")))

rules.name: Liechtenstein: in principle no source tax liability
rules.statement: Liechtenstein residents are asked the source tax questions (HR's rule). With daily return, or without daily return and at most 45 non-return days, the result is 'in principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement' instead of a tariff code, flagged for HR, and the remaining tariff questions are skipped. With more than 45 non-return days the normal tariff code applies with the note 'subject to the double taxation agreement', flagged for HR (assumption D-040).

table.then: In principle no source tax liability
In principle no source tax liability
Normal tariff code, subject to the double taxation agreement

rules.statement: Married and Registered partnership count as 'married or registered partnership'; Single, Divorced, Widowed and Separated count as 'single, divorced, separated or widowed', as in the calculator.
rules.expression: if_else(civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"], "Married or registered partnership", if_else(civil_status in ["Single", "Divorced", "Widowed", "Separated"], "Single, divorced, separated or widowed", null))

rules.statement: The country of residence is grouped as in the calculator: Switzerland, Germany, Liechtenstein or other country. Switzerland and other country lead to the base tariff without further residence questions.

rules.statement: Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed gives suffix Y; none or other gives N.

when: Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed

rules.expression: if_else(confession == "Roman Catholic, Christian Catholic or Evangelical Reformed", "Y", if_else(confession == "None or other", "N", null))

rules.name: Per-child source tax result
rules.statement: For each child, the answers give one of: counted, counted with H (single parents), or not counted - following the calculator. Observed calculator rows win over the derived logic (assumption D-046); rows marked inferred are not observed and are checked before go-live (D-009).
rules.expression: if_else(child_age_status == "Neither", "not counted", if_else(calculator_civil_status == "Married or registered partnership", if_else(child_age_status == "Minor", if_else(child_same_household == "yes", if_else(child_custody == "Sole custody" or child_common_household_other_parent == "yes" or (child_alternating_custody == "yes" and child_main_financial_contributor == "Me"), "counted", "not counted"), if_else(child_shared_custody == "yes" and child_alternating_custody == "yes" and child_main_financial_contributor == "Me", "counted", "not counted")), if_else(child_common_household_other_parent == "yes" or child_maintenance_over_50 == "yes", "counted", "not counted")), if_else(child_age_status == "Minor", if_else(child_same_household == "yes", if_else(child_custody == "Sole custody" or child_main_financial_contributor == "Me" or (child_common_household_other_parent == "no" and child_alternating_custody == "no"), "counted with H", "not counted"), if_else(child_parental_care == "yes" and child_alternating_custody == "yes" and child_main_financial_contributor == "Me", "counted with H", "not counted")), if_else(child_same_household == "yes", if_else(child_main_financial_contributor == "Me" or child_maintenance_over_50 == "yes", "counted with H", "not counted"), if_else(child_maintenance_over_50 == "yes", "counted", "not counted")))))

rules.name: Child digit of the tariff code
rules.statement: The child digit equals the number of children whose per-child result is 'counted' or 'counted with H' (e.g. three counted children give C3Y). Without children the digit is 0. (The expression gives, per child, whether that child is counted; the digit is the number of children for which it is true.)

rules.name: Base tariff letter
rules.statement: Married/registered partners: C if the spouse is gainfully employed, otherwise B. Single, divorced, separated or widowed: H if at least one child is counted with H, otherwise A.
inputs: At least one child counted with H
rules.expression: if_else(calculator_civil_status == "Married or registered partnership", if_else(spouse_gainful_employment == "yes", "C", "B"), if_else(child_result == "counted with H", "H", "A"))

rules.name: Cross-border tariff applies (Germany)
rules.statement: For Germany residents the cross-border tariff applies with daily return and a certificate of residence ('not yet' counts as no), or without daily return when daily return is reasonable and the employee does not expect more than 60 non-return days. Otherwise the normal tariff applies. Other countries never get the cross-border tariff.
rules.expression: address_country == "Germany" and ((daily_return_germany == "yes" and residence_certificate == "yes") or (daily_return_germany == "no" and daily_return_reasonable == "yes" and non_return_days_60 == "no"))

rules.name: Tariff letter
rules.statement: Without the cross-border tariff the base letter applies. With it: A becomes L, B becomes M, C becomes N, H becomes P (and G would become Q, as the calculator shows; G does not occur because replacement income is out of scope, D-006).
rules.expression: if_else(cross_border_tariff, if_else(base_tariff_letter == "A", "L", if_else(base_tariff_letter == "B", "M", if_else(base_tariff_letter == "C", "N", if_else(base_tariff_letter == "H", "P", if_else(base_tariff_letter == "G", "Q", null))))), base_tariff_letter)

rules.name: Source tax tariff code
rules.statement: Lonio computes the full Zurich tariff code for every employee subject to source tax, replacing HR's manual calculator step: one text made of tariff letter, child digit and church-tax suffix, e.g. 'C1Y', 'L0Y', 'N1Y'. Employees not subject to source tax get 'no tariff code'. Liechtenstein residents with in principle no liability get 'in principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement', flagged for HR; with more than 45 non-return days the code carries the note 'subject to the double taxation agreement', flagged for HR. If HR later changes an answer so that unanswered questions apply, the result is 'incomplete - HR must complete' until HR enters them (assumption D-048). Always derived again from the latest answers. Computed codes are not legally binding, like the calculator's.
inputs: In principle no source tax liability

table.then: 'in principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement', flagged for HR
Full tariff code with note 'subject to the double taxation agreement', flagged for HR
Full tariff code (letter + child digit + church-tax suffix)

rules.expression: if_else(not subject_to_source_tax, "no tariff code", if_else(liechtenstein_no_source_tax, "in principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement", [tariff_letter, if_else(child_count, 1, 0), church_tax_suffix]))

rules.name: Permit reminder
rules.statement: At the end of the questionnaire, every non-Swiss employee living in Switzerland and every employee living abroad (whatever their nationality, which is not asked of them) is reminded to bring their permit on the first working day. HR provides the wording before go-live, worded so that a Swiss citizen living abroad sees it does not apply to them. It collects no data.

rules.name: Discard answers that no longer apply
rules.statement: Answers to questions that no longer apply after an earlier answer changes are kept while the employee goes back and forth, and discarded on submission. The same applies when HR changes an answer after submission (D-048).

rules.name: Read-only after submission
rules.statement: After submission the questionnaire is read-only for the employee. Later changes (a move, marriage, new child, a certificate of residence handed in later, a corrected nationality, a moved first working day) are made by HR (specified later). All derived results are always derived again from the latest answers.

feature.title: Employee onboarding questionnaire
feature.goal: A new employee of Muster AG answers one questionnaire, in English, that asks each piece of information once and only when a receiving party needs it. From those answers Lonio records what the pension fund needs to register the employee, what HR needs for its records, and the full Zurich source tax tariff code, with no manual calculator step.
feature.context: Today the onboarding data is collected for each receiving party separately. HR then re-enters it in Pensionskasse Muster's portal and clicks through the Zurich source tax calculator to find the tariff. If too little is asked, a registration is blocked: for example, the fund requires the spouse's date of birth for married employees. If too much is asked, Lonio holds personal data no party needs, which breaks data minimisation (G-01). The receiving parties in scope are the pension fund, source tax and HR (G-02). Social insurance (AHV) data, IT equipment and badge photos are out of scope (G-03). This spec covers only what the employee is asked, in which order and under which conditions, plus the rules derived from the answers. How data is sent to each party and any HR screens are separate topics (G-04, D-034). Lonio derives values instead of asking for them where it can (G-08), for example the insurance start date (D-039) and the full tariff code (D-001, D-051). The questionnaire has eight fixed steps (D-047). It is read-only for the employee after submission; HR makes later changes, and every derived result is always derived again from the latest answers (D-033, D-037, D-048). The sources are fictional and are treated as the truth (G-06). Where a decision is marked as an assumption, the story must state it for a domain expert to verify.

sections.title: Questionnaire flow overview
sections.purpose: Define the eight steps, their order and the conditions under which each step and question appears. Cover saving and resuming, going back without losing answers, discarding answers that no longer apply, the permit reminder, the summary and confirmation, and read-only after submission.

stories.title: Show the source tax step only to employees who are subject to source tax
stories.i_want: the source tax details (denomination, whether the spouse is gainfully employed, whether there are children) and the children step to be asked only of employees who are subject to source tax, and for Liechtenstein residents only when they stay abroad more than 45 non-return days
stories.so_that: I no longer have to guess up front who must answer the source tax questions, and Lonio holds no source tax data about people who do not need it
stories.priority_reason: HR names this as a current pain ('I never know up front who has to answer those questions'), and asking everyone breaks data minimisation (G-01).

acceptance_criteria.title: Source tax details only for employees subject to source tax
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has answered the steps 'Home address', 'Nationality and C permit' and 'Civil status and spouse'
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio decides whether to show step 6 'Source tax details'
acceptance_criteria.then: the step is shown only if the employee is subject to source tax (anyone living abroad; or, living in Switzerland, a non-Swiss employee without a C permit who is not married or in a registered partnership with a Swiss national or C-permit holder living in Switzerland). Otherwise denomination, spouse gainfully employed and has children are not asked, and step 7 'Children' is not shown either.

examples.name: Stefan, Swiss living abroad, country assumed Germany (hr_transcript/F-hr_transcript-3f2c2a)
Non-Swiss, no C permit, single, living in Switzerland
Non-Swiss in a registered partnership with a non-Swiss partner without C permit

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse gainfully employed only for married employees and registered partners
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee is shown step 6 'Source tax details'
acceptance_criteria.when: the step is shown
acceptance_criteria.then: the question whether the spouse or registered partner is gainfully employed is asked only if the civil status is Married or Registered partnership; Separated counts as single for source tax, so separated, single, divorced and widowed employees are not asked it (assumption D-003, to be verified by a domain expert).

acceptance_criteria.title: Liechtenstein residents: cross-border questions first, tariff questions only above 45 non-return days
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee lives in Liechtenstein (and is therefore subject to source tax)
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee goes through the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: step 5 'Cross-border commuting' (daily return, then more than 45 non-return days) comes before step 6 'Source tax details'. If the employee returns daily or expects at most 45 non-return days, there is in principle no source tax liability and steps 6 and 7 are skipped. If the employee expects more than 45 non-return days, steps 6 and 7 are asked as for any employee subject to source tax. Assumption (to be verified by a domain expert): this order and skipping follow D-040.

examples.name: Liechtenstein, no daily return, at most 45 days
Liechtenstein, no daily return, more than 45 days

stories.title: Ask the steps in an order that avoids unneeded questions
stories.i_want: to go through eight fixed steps in a fixed order, where each step and each question appears only when a receiving party needs my answer
stories.so_that: I answer only what is needed, and earlier answers (where I live, my nationality, my civil status) decide which later questions I see
stories.priority_reason: The flow is the backbone of the questionnaire: asking too little blocks a registration, asking too much collects personal data no party needs (G-01).

acceptance_criteria.title: Exactly eight steps in a fixed order
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee opens the questionnaire, which is in English
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee goes through it
acceptance_criteria.then: the steps come in this order: 1 About you; 2 Home address; 3 Nationality and C permit; 4 Civil status and spouse; 5 Cross-border commuting; 6 Source tax details; 7 Children; 8 Permit reminder, summary and submission. There is no separate step for the first working day. A step whose questions all do not apply to this employee is skipped. Assumption (to be verified by a domain expert): this list of steps and its order follow D-047.

acceptance_criteria.title: Step 1 'About you' for everyone
acceptance_criteria.given: any employee
acceptance_criteria.when: step 1 is shown
acceptance_criteria.then: first name, last name, date of birth and first working day are required of everyone.

acceptance_criteria.title: Step 2 'Home address' as on the first working day; canton only in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: any employee
acceptance_criteria.when: step 2 is shown
acceptance_criteria.then: the home address as it applies on the first working day is required: street, house number (or the explicit option 'no house number'), postcode, town and country. The canton is asked only if the country is Switzerland. Assumptions (to be verified by a domain expert): the address applies on the first working day (D-041), every address field is required apart from the 'no house number' option (D-042, D-049), and employees abroad are not asked for a canton (D-002).

examples.name: Stefan, Swiss living abroad, country assumed Germany (hr_transcript/F-hr_transcript-3f2c2a)

acceptance_criteria.title: Step 3 'Nationality and C permit' only for employees living in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has given the country of the home address
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio decides whether to show step 3
acceptance_criteria.then: nationality is asked only if the employee lives in Switzerland; employees living abroad are subject to source tax whatever their nationality and are not asked it. Whether the employee holds a C permit (yes/no) is asked only if the nationality is not Switzerland; no other permit type is asked. Anyone holding Swiss citizenship, also together with another nationality, answers Switzerland.

examples.name: Stefan, Swiss living abroad, country assumed Germany (hr_transcript/F-hr_transcript-3f2c2a)

acceptance_criteria.title: Step 4 'Civil status and spouse': civil status for everyone, spouse questions only when needed
acceptance_criteria.given: any employee, wherever they live
acceptance_criteria.when: step 4 is shown
acceptance_criteria.then: civil status is required of everyone. The spouse's or registered partner's date of birth is asked only if the civil status is Married, Registered partnership or Separated, not if Divorced or Widowed (assumption D-004, to be verified by a domain expert). The spouse's nationality, whether the spouse holds a C permit (only if the spouse is not Swiss) and whether the spouse lives in Switzerland (only if the spouse is Swiss or holds a C permit) are asked only of a non-Swiss employee living in Switzerland without a C permit who is married or in a registered partnership, because only then can the spouse exemption from source tax apply.

acceptance_criteria.title: Step 5 'Cross-border commuting' only for Liechtenstein and Germany residents
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has given the country of the home address
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio decides whether to show step 5
acceptance_criteria.then: the step is shown only to employees living in Liechtenstein or Germany, who are all subject to source tax. Liechtenstein residents are asked about daily return and, without daily return, about more than 45 non-return days; Germany residents are asked about daily return and the follow-up questions (including the certificate of residence). The employee states what they expect for the year; no documents are uploaded. Employees living in Switzerland or in any other country do not see this step.

acceptance_criteria.title: Steps 6 and 7 only when source tax details apply; one block per child
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee is subject to source tax and, if living in Liechtenstein, expects more than 45 non-return days
acceptance_criteria.when: steps 6 and 7 are shown
acceptance_criteria.then: step 6 asks denomination, spouse gainfully employed (married and registered partners only) and whether the employee has biological or adopted children. Step 7 'Children' is shown only if the answer is yes, with one block of child questions per child; there is no maximum number of children and each child's age is judged on the first working day (assumption D-044, to be verified by a domain expert).

acceptance_criteria.title: Step 8 closes the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has answered every step that applies
acceptance_criteria.when: step 8 is shown
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee sees the permit reminder if it applies to them, then a summary page, and submits with one confirmation.

stories.title: Ask each piece of information once and reuse it for every receiving party
stories.i_want: each piece of information to be asked once in the questionnaire and recorded for every receiving party that needs it (pension fund, source tax and HR)
stories.so_that: the employee is not asked the same thing twice and I no longer collect the data separately for each party and re-enter it
stories.priority_reason: Core goal of the feature (G-01): collect once, reuse for every party; today data is collected per party and re-entered manually.

acceptance_criteria.title: No question appears twice
acceptance_criteria.given: a piece of information is needed by more than one party (for example civil status by the pension fund and for source tax, or the country of residence by HR, the pension fund and source tax)
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee goes through the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: the question is asked once, in its step, and the single answer is recorded for HR and used for every party that needs it; for example civil status is asked once in step 4 and serves both the pension fund registration and the source tax tariff.

examples.name: Civil status asked once for everyone

acceptance_criteria.title: Derived values are not asked
acceptance_criteria.given: a value one party needs can be derived from answers already given
acceptance_criteria.when: the questionnaire is shown
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is not asked for it: the insurance start date is derived from the first working day, the canton for employees living abroad is set to the canton of the place of work (Zurich), the civil status for the pension fund and for source tax is derived from the one civil status answer, and the source tax tariff code is computed from the answers. Assumption (to be verified by a domain expert): the canton for employees abroad follows D-002 and the civil status mapping follows D-003.

acceptance_criteria.title: Answers are recorded for HR
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has submitted the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: the answers are recorded
acceptance_criteria.then: they are recorded for HR; how they are passed to the pension fund and the source tax office, and any HR screen, are specified separately.

stories.title: Remind non-Swiss employees and employees living abroad to bring their permit
stories.i_want: every non-Swiss employee living in Switzerland and every employee living abroad to be reminded at the end of the questionnaire to bring their permit on the first working day
stories.so_that: fewer new employees forget their permit on their first day
stories.priority_reason: Explicit HR wish ('Half of them forget'); it saves follow-up but does not block a registration.

acceptance_criteria.title: Who sees the reminder
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee reaches step 8 'Permit reminder, summary and submission'
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio decides whether to show the permit reminder
acceptance_criteria.then: the reminder is shown to an employee living in Switzerland whose nationality is not Switzerland, and to every employee living abroad whatever their nationality (nationality is not asked of them). It is not shown to a Swiss employee living in Switzerland.

examples.name: Stefan, Swiss living abroad, country assumed Germany (hr_transcript/F-hr_transcript-3f2c2a)

acceptance_criteria.title: Wording provided by HR; Swiss citizens abroad can tell it does not apply
acceptance_criteria.given: the reminder is shown
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reads it
acceptance_criteria.then: it uses the wording HR provides before go-live, and that wording lets a Swiss citizen living abroad, such as Stefan, see that it does not apply to them. The reminder only informs: it asks no question and collects no data.

stories.title: Discard answers that no longer apply on submission
stories.i_want: to go back and change an earlier answer without losing my other answers, while answers to questions that no longer apply are not kept once I submit
stories.so_that: I can correct myself freely, and Lonio keeps no personal data about me that no party needs
stories.priority_reason: Data minimisation is a hard constraint (G-01); losing input when going back would frustrate employees.

acceptance_criteria.title: Going back keeps answers until submission
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has answered questions in later steps and goes back to change an earlier answer so that some of those questions no longer apply
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee changes the answer back, or moves forward again, before submitting
acceptance_criteria.then: every answer given earlier is still there, including answers to questions that currently do not apply, so no input is lost by going back and forth before submission.

acceptance_criteria.title: Answers that no longer apply are discarded on submission
acceptance_criteria.given: at submission some answers belong to questions that do not apply to the employee's latest answers
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee submits
acceptance_criteria.then: those answers are discarded and are not recorded, shown on the record or used for any result; only answers to questions that apply are kept.

examples.name: Moved the home address from Germany to Switzerland before submitting; Germany cross-border and source tax answers are discarded
Changed civil status from Married to Divorced before submitting; spouse date of birth is discarded

stories.title: Make the questionnaire read-only after submission and derive results from the latest answers
stories.i_want: the questionnaire to be read-only for the employee once submitted, with later changes made by HR and every derived result always derived again from the latest answers
stories.so_that: the record stays consistent and the pension fund and source tax always get results that match the current facts
stories.priority_reason: Prevents inconsistent records after submission; the HR editing itself is specified later (D-034).

acceptance_criteria.title: Read-only for the employee after submission
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has submitted the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee opens it again
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee can see the answers but cannot change them; any later change (a move, a marriage, a new child, a certificate of residence handed in later, a corrected nationality, a moved first working day) is made by HR, in the HR-side spec to be written later.

acceptance_criteria.title: Derived results always follow the latest answers
acceptance_criteria.given: an answer has changed after submission
acceptance_criteria.when: the derived results are looked at
acceptance_criteria.then: the insurance start date, the civil status for the pension fund and for source tax, whether the employee is subject to source tax and the tariff code are derived again from the latest answers; for the first working day the latest date always counts and no history of earlier dates is kept.

examples.name: Tomás after HR records that his wife no longer lives in Switzerland

acceptance_criteria.title: HR change that opens unanswered questions
acceptance_criteria.given: after submission HR changes an answer so that questions apply that the employee was never asked (for example the employee now becomes subject to source tax)
acceptance_criteria.when: the derived results that depend on those questions are looked at
acceptance_criteria.then: they show 'incomplete - HR must complete' instead of a value (for example the tariff code) until HR enters the missing answers. Assumption (to be verified by a domain expert): this follows D-048.

acceptance_criteria.title: HR change that makes answers no longer apply
acceptance_criteria.given: after submission HR changes an answer so that some recorded answers no longer apply
acceptance_criteria.when: HR's change is saved
acceptance_criteria.then: the answers that no longer apply are discarded, as on the employee's submission. Assumption (to be verified by a domain expert): this follows D-048.

stories.title: Save answers as I go and resume until I submit
stories.i_want: my answers to be saved as I go, so that I can stop and come back to the questionnaire until I submit it
stories.so_that: I can look up information (for example my spouse's date of birth or my expected non-return days) without losing what I have already entered
stories.priority_reason: Convenience for the employee; it does not change which data is collected.

acceptance_criteria.title: Answers are saved as the employee goes
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has answered some questions and leaves the questionnaire before submitting
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee returns
acceptance_criteria.then: all answers given so far are still there and the employee can continue and submit. Assumption (to be verified by a domain expert): this follows D-050.

acceptance_criteria.title: Resuming ends with submission
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has submitted the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee returns
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee can no longer change answers; the questionnaire is read-only and later changes are made by HR.

stories.title: Review a summary and submit with one confirmation
stories.i_want: to see a summary of my answers and submit them with one confirmation
stories.so_that: I can check what I give before it is recorded for HR and used for the pension fund and source tax
stories.priority_reason: Submission completes the onboarding data; without it no registration or tariff code can be produced.

acceptance_criteria.title: Summary before submission
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has answered every step that applies and has seen the permit reminder if it applies
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches the end of step 8
acceptance_criteria.then: a summary page shows the employee's answers. Assumption (to be verified by a domain expert): the summary shows only answers to questions that apply to the employee's latest answers, since the others will be discarded on submission (D-036, D-045).

acceptance_criteria.title: One confirmation submits
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee is on the summary page
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee confirms once
acceptance_criteria.then: the questionnaire is submitted and the answers are recorded for HR; nothing is submitted before this confirmation.

acceptance_criteria.title: Required answers must be given before submission
acceptance_criteria.given: a question that applies and is required for this employee has no answer
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee tries to submit
acceptance_criteria.then: the questionnaire is not submitted and the employee is shown which answers are missing. Assumption (to be verified by a domain expert): no source states this behaviour explicitly; it follows from the questions being required (D-045).

sections.title: Personal details and home address
sections.purpose: Collect the employee's name, date of birth and complete home address (as on the first working day), plus the canton for the pension fund. Residents of Switzerland choose their canton; for employees abroad Zurich is recorded and the canton is not asked.

stories.title: Collect the employee's name and date of birth
stories.i_want: every new employee to give their first name, last name and date of birth in the first step 'About you' of the onboarding questionnaire
stories.so_that: the registration at Pensionskasse Muster is never blocked by an empty required field (First name, Last name, Date of birth), and HR can identify the employee and address documents to them
stories.priority_reason: The pension fund portal rejects a registration when First name, Last name or Date of birth is empty, so without them the registration is blocked.

acceptance_criteria.title: First and last name are always asked and required
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee fills in step 1 'About you' of the questionnaire (the step also holds the first working day, which another story covers), whatever they answer elsewhere
acceptance_criteria.when: they try to continue without a first name or a last name
acceptance_criteria.then: they cannot continue until both are filled in. The first and last name are recorded for the pension fund (its required fields 'First name' and 'Last name') and for HR, which uses the name to identify the employee and address documents. HR's need for the name is inferred: HR confirmed 'name, address' but only explained the address.

examples.name: Employee living abroad: name required too

acceptance_criteria.title: Date of birth is always asked and required, as DD.MM.YYYY
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee fills in step 1 'About you'
acceptance_criteria.when: they enter their date of birth
acceptance_criteria.then: the date of birth is required for every employee and is given as a date in the form DD.MM.YYYY (e.g. 14.03.1990). It is recorded for the pension fund, whose registration form requires 'Date of birth' in that form.

examples.name: Any employee: date of birth required

acceptance_criteria.title: Date of birth must be plausible for the first working day
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee has entered a date of birth and a first working day
acceptance_criteria.when: the date of birth means they would be younger than 14 or older than 100 on the first working day
acceptance_criteria.then: the date of birth is not accepted and the employee is asked to correct it. An employee who is at least 14 and at most 100 years old on the first working day can continue. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-050): these age limits are a product decision, not stated by the pension fund or HR.

acceptance_criteria.title: No further personal identifiers are asked
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee fills in step 1 'About you'
acceptance_criteria.when: they look at the questions in the step
acceptance_criteria.then: besides the first working day, only first name, last name and date of birth are asked. No social insurance (AHV) number and no badge photo are asked, because no receiving party in scope needs them.

stories.title: Collect a complete postal home address
stories.i_want: every new employee to give a complete postal home address (street, house number, postcode, town and country) as it will be on their first working day, in step 2 'Home address'
stories.so_that: the many documents HR posts to employees reach them, without HR having to chase missing parts of the address
stories.priority_reason: HR posts many documents to employees and states the address 'has to be complete'; an incomplete address stops HR's postal correspondence.

acceptance_criteria.title: Street, postcode and town are required for every employee
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee fills in step 2 'Home address', wherever they live
acceptance_criteria.when: they try to continue with the street, the postcode or the town empty
acceptance_criteria.then: they cannot continue until street, postcode and town are filled in. The address is recorded for HR. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-049): every home address field is required; the only exception is the explicit 'no house number' option.

acceptance_criteria.title: House number is required, with an explicit 'no house number' option
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee fills in step 2 'Home address'
acceptance_criteria.when: they try to continue without a house number
acceptance_criteria.then: they can continue only if they have entered a house number or explicitly chosen 'no house number'; an empty house number alone is not accepted. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-042): HR wants the address complete including the number, and some addresses have no house number.

examples.name: House number required for any employee

acceptance_criteria.title: The address is the one that applies on the first working day
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee will move before their first working day
acceptance_criteria.when: they fill in step 2 'Home address'
acceptance_criteria.then: the question makes clear that the address asked is the one that applies on the first working day, so the employee enters their new address. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-041).

acceptance_criteria.title: Only a normal postal address is asked
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee fills in step 2 'Home address'
acceptance_criteria.when: they look at the address questions
acceptance_criteria.then: only what is needed to write the address on an envelope is asked: street, house number, postcode, town and country. Nothing else, such as a second address or a phone number, is asked.

stories.title: Use the home address country as the country of residence
stories.i_want: the country of the employee's home address to count as their country of residence, without a separate residence question
stories.so_that: Lonio knows whether the employee lives in Switzerland or abroad. Employees living abroad are always subject to source tax, and the country decides which later questions apply. The employee is asked for the country only once.
stories.priority_reason: The country of residence decides source tax liability and the canton for the pension fund; without it neither the tariff nor the registration can be completed.

acceptance_criteria.title: Country is required and chosen from the country list
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee fills in step 2 'Home address'
acceptance_criteria.when: they give the country of their home address as it applies on the first working day
acceptance_criteria.then: the country is required and is chosen from the ISO 3166 country list, shown by English name (e.g. Switzerland, Germany, Liechtenstein). This country is the employee's country of residence; no separate question about the country of residence is asked. It is recorded for HR as part of the postal address, for source tax and for the pension fund (the fund uses it to decide the canton). Assumptions to be verified by a domain expert: the country list (D-050) and the address as on the first working day (D-041).

acceptance_criteria.title: Employees living abroad are subject to source tax and are not asked nationality or canton
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee's home address on the first working day is outside Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: they continue the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: they are subject to source tax whatever their nationality (HR's example: Stefan is Swiss, lives abroad and is still subject). Their nationality is not asked (data minimisation), and the canton is not asked either. 'Here' in HR's rule is read as Switzerland; assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-043).

examples.name: Stefan, Swiss, living abroad (hr_transcript/F-hr_transcript-3f2c2a; country assumed)

acceptance_criteria.title: Employees living in Switzerland are asked their nationality and canton
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee's home address on the first working day is in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: they continue the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked their canton of residence in step 2 and their nationality in step 3 'Nationality and C permit'. Whether they are subject to source tax then depends on those later answers, not on the country alone.

stories.title: Ask Swiss residents for their canton
stories.i_want: a canton for every new employee: the canton of residence chosen by employees who live in Switzerland, and Zurich (the canton of the place of work at Muster AG) for employees who live abroad, without asking them
stories.so_that: the required 'Canton' field of the registration is always filled, even for employees living abroad, for whom the fund's list has no option
stories.priority_reason: 'Canton' is a required field of the fund's registration; if it is empty the registration is rejected ('Canton is required.').

acceptance_criteria.title: Employees living in Switzerland choose their canton
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee's home address on the first working day is in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: they fill in step 2 'Home address'
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked their canton of residence, it is required, and they choose one of the 26 cantons the fund lists: Aargau, Appenzell Ausserrhoden, Appenzell Innerrhoden, Basel-Landschaft, Basel-Stadt, Bern, Fribourg, Geneva, Glarus, Graubünden, Jura, Lucerne, Neuchâtel, Nidwalden, Obwalden, Schaffhausen, Schwyz, Solothurn, St. Gallen, Thurgau, Ticino, Uri, Valais, Vaud, Zug, Zurich. The chosen canton is recorded as the canton for the pension fund.

acceptance_criteria.title: Employees living abroad are not asked; Zurich is recorded
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee's home address on the first working day is outside Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: they fill in step 2 'Home address'
acceptance_criteria.then: the canton is not asked, and Zurich, the canton of the place of work at Muster AG, is recorded as the canton for the pension fund. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-002): the fund's portal does not say whether 'Canton' means residence or place of work, and its list has no option for a residence abroad.

acceptance_criteria.title: The canton for the fund always follows the latest answers
acceptance_criteria.given: the questionnaire has been submitted and HR later changes the employee's country of residence
acceptance_criteria.when: the canton for the pension fund is derived again
acceptance_criteria.then: it follows the latest answers. If the employee now lives abroad, Zurich is recorded and any canton chosen earlier is discarded. If the employee now lives in Switzerland but no canton was ever asked, the canton for the fund shows 'incomplete - HR must complete' until HR enters it. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-048). How HR makes the change belongs to the later HR-side spec.

sections.title: First working day and insurance start date
sections.purpose: Ask for the first working day (the contractual start date) in step 1, without a separate step, and derive the pension fund's insurance start date from it.

stories.title: Employee confirms the first working day
stories.i_want: to enter my first working day in the first step of the onboarding questionnaire, 'About you'
stories.so_that: the pension fund and HR use the start date I actually agreed on, including when it moved after I signed my contract
stories.priority_reason: HR calls the first working day 'the number one thing' for the pension fund, and it often moves (F-hr_transcript-872bd7, F-hr_transcript-e3721e). Without it the fund registration is blocked.

acceptance_criteria.title: First working day is asked of and required from every employee in step 1
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee fills in the onboarding questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: they complete step 1 'About you' (first name, last name, date of birth, first working day)
acceptance_criteria.then: the first working day is asked of and required from every employee, whatever their residence, nationality or civil status. It is part of step 1, and the questionnaire has no separate step for it. Assumption, to be verified by a domain expert: the eight-step order in D-047.

acceptance_criteria.title: First working day is the contractual start date
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee whose contractual start date falls on a weekend or a public holiday
acceptance_criteria.when: they enter their first working day
acceptance_criteria.then: they enter the contractual start date as is, and it is accepted even on a weekend or public holiday. The questionnaire explains that the contractual start date is meant. Assumption, to be verified by a domain expert: the first working day is the contractual start date (D-039).

acceptance_criteria.title: Allowed form and range of the first working day
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee enters their first working day
acceptance_criteria.when: the date is checked
acceptance_criteria.then: the first working day is a calendar date written as DD.MM.YYYY. It must lie within one year after the questionnaire was sent; if it does not, the employee is told the date is not accepted and cannot continue until they correct it. Assumption, to be verified by a domain expert: the one-year limit comes from D-050.

acceptance_criteria.title: Who receives the first working day
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has submitted the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: the answers are recorded
acceptance_criteria.then: the first working day is recorded for the pension fund, as the basis of the insurance start date, and for HR, which plans the start and keeps the fund registration up to date. The employee is not asked for the insurance start date.

acceptance_criteria.title: Only HR changes the first working day after submission
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has submitted the questionnaire and their start date later moves
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee wants to change the first working day
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee cannot change it in the questionnaire, which is read-only after submission. Only HR can change the date; how HR does this is specified in the later HR-side spec. The latest date always counts, and no history of earlier dates is kept.

stories.title: Derive the pension insurance start date from the first working day
stories.i_want: to receive an insurance start date on the 1st of a month, derived from the employee's first working day
stories.so_that: the registration's required 'Insurance start date' is valid without the employee having to know or work out the fund's rule
stories.priority_reason: The 'Insurance start date' is a required field of the fund registration and must be the 1st of a month (F-pension_portal-509cbe, F-pension_portal-dd8126). A wrong date led to an unfriendly letter and weeks of fixing (F-hr_transcript-e18e66).

acceptance_criteria.title: Insurance start date is derived, never asked
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee fills in the onboarding questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: they go through all steps
acceptance_criteria.then: they are never asked for the insurance start date. Lonio derives it from the first working day and records it for the pension fund as a date in the format DD.MM.YYYY that is always the 1st of a month.

acceptance_criteria.title: First working day on the 1st of a month
acceptance_criteria.given: the first working day is the 1st of a month
acceptance_criteria.when: the insurance start date is derived
acceptance_criteria.then: insurance starts on the first working day itself. This also applies when that day is a weekend or public holiday, because the first working day is the contractual start date. Assumption, to be verified by a domain expert: see D-039.

acceptance_criteria.title: First working day on any other day
acceptance_criteria.given: the first working day is not the 1st of a month
acceptance_criteria.when: the insurance start date is derived
acceptance_criteria.then: insurance starts on the 1st of the following month, including across a year end.

stories.title: Re-derive the insurance start date when the first working day moves
stories.i_want: the insurance start date to be derived again every time the first working day changes
stories.so_that: the date at the pension fund never drifts from the actual start date, as it did for Julia
stories.priority_reason: A missed update after Julia's start date moved caused a wrong date at the fund, an unfriendly letter and weeks of fixing (F-hr_transcript-e18e66). Start dates move often (F-hr_transcript-e3721e).

acceptance_criteria.title: Insurance start date always follows the latest first working day
acceptance_criteria.given: the first working day was changed, either by the employee before submission or by HR after submission
acceptance_criteria.when: the insurance start date is derived
acceptance_criteria.then: it is derived from the latest first working day only. Earlier dates and the insurance start dates derived from them are not kept. How the changed date reaches the pension fund belongs to the separate transmission and HR-side topics.

sections.title: Civil status and spouse data
sections.purpose: Ask every employee for their civil status, using six values. Map it to the pension fund's four values and to the calculator's two groups. Ask the spouse's or registered partner's date of birth only of married, registered-partner and separated employees.

stories.title: Ask every employee for their civil status
stories.i_want: to state my civil status once, in step 4 'Civil status and spouse' of the onboarding questionnaire, choosing from a list that matches my real situation
stories.so_that: Lonio can register me with the pension fund and work out my source tax tariff without asking me the same thing again for each party
stories.priority_reason: The pension fund requires a civil status to register the employee, and the source tax tariff depends on it. Without it, the registration and the tariff are blocked.

acceptance_criteria.title: Civil status is asked of everyone and is required
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee is filling in the questionnaire, wherever they live
acceptance_criteria.when: they reach step 4 'Civil status and spouse'
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked for their civil status and cannot submit the questionnaire without answering. The answer is recorded for the pension fund and for source tax. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert: the step order follows the agreed eight-step list (D-047).

acceptance_criteria.title: Six civil status values are offered
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee is asked for their civil status
acceptance_criteria.when: they choose an answer
acceptance_criteria.then: they can choose exactly one of: Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed, Registered partnership, Separated. The fund's list has only the first four. Registered partnership and Separated are added because the source tax calculator treats them in a specific way and registered partnerships do occur at Muster AG. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-003).

stories.title: Ask for the spouse's or registered partner's date of birth when the fund registers the employee as Married
stories.i_want: to receive the spouse's date of birth for every employee registered with me as Married
stories.so_that: the registration is not blocked by a missing required field
stories.priority_reason: The fund's portal blocks the registration with 'Spouse's date of birth is required.' when the civil status is Married and the field is empty.

acceptance_criteria.title: Asked and required only of married, registered-partner and separated employees
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has answered the civil status question in step 4
acceptance_criteria.when: the civil status is Married, Registered partnership or Separated
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked for the date of birth of their spouse or registered partner and must answer it. For Single, Divorced or Widowed it is not asked, and no spouse data is sent to the fund. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-004): the fund needs the date of birth for everyone it registers as Married, which includes registered partners and separated employees (D-003). It also assumes the fund needs nothing extra for Divorced or Widowed (see OQ-fund-divorced-widowed).

acceptance_criteria.title: Date of birth given as a full date
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee is asked for the spouse's or registered partner's date of birth
acceptance_criteria.when: they enter it
acceptance_criteria.then: it is accepted only as a complete date in the form DD.MM.YYYY, as the fund requires, and is recorded for the pension fund.

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse's date of birth discarded when it no longer applies
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee entered a spouse's date of birth and then changed their civil status to Single, Divorced or Widowed
acceptance_criteria.when: they submit the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: the spouse's date of birth is not kept. Before submission, it is kept so that the employee loses no input if they change the civil status back.

stories.title: Answer the calculator's civil status question from the employee's civil status
stories.i_want: the employee's civil status to be put into the calculator's two groups the same way the Zurich calculator does it
stories.so_that: the computed tariff code uses the right civil status group without anyone clicking through the calculator
stories.priority_reason: The full tariff code is computed by Lonio and replaces HR's manual calculator step (D-001). A wrong group gives a wrong tariff.

acceptance_criteria.title: Civil status mapped to the calculator's two groups
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has answered the civil status question
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio works out the civil status for source tax
acceptance_criteria.then: Married and Registered partnership count as 'Married or registered partnership'. Single, Divorced, Widowed and Separated count as 'Single, divorced, separated or widowed'. This follows the calculator's two options. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert: a registered partnership is treated as married, including the spouse exemption, and Separated is treated as single (D-003). The result is always worked out again from the latest civil status, including after HR changes it (D-037).

stories.title: Enter the civil status on the pension fund's list
stories.i_want: to receive the employee's civil status as one of the four values my registration form accepts
stories.so_that: the employee can be registered for occupational pension without HR having to interpret the answer
stories.priority_reason: The fund's civil status field is required and accepts only Single, Married, Divorced or Widowed. Any other value blocks the registration.

acceptance_criteria.title: Civil status mapped to the fund's four values
acceptance_criteria.given: an employee has answered the civil status question
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio works out the civil status for the pension fund
acceptance_criteria.then: Single, Married, Divorced and Widowed stay as they are. Registered partnership and Separated are recorded as Married, together with the spouse's or partner's date of birth. HR did not know how the fund handles a registered partnership, so this is an assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-003). Whether the fund needs an extra field for Divorced or Widowed is still open (see OQ-fund-divorced-widowed). The result is always worked out again from the latest civil status, including after HR changes it (D-037).

sections.title: Who is subject to source tax
sections.purpose: Decide whether the employee is subject to source tax. Ask nationality and C permit only of residents of Switzerland. Ask the spouse's nationality, C permit and residence only when needed to check the spouse exemption.

stories.title: Ask nationality and C permit only of employees living in Switzerland
stories.i_want: to be asked my nationality and, if I am not Swiss, only whether I hold a C permit - and only when I live in Switzerland
stories.so_that: Lonio can decide whether I am subject to source tax without collecting nationality or permit data that no receiving party needs for me (data minimisation)
stories.priority_reason: Source tax liability cannot be decided for residents of Switzerland without these answers; HR names nationality and the C permit as the deciding facts (F-hr_transcript-5af8d0, F-hr_transcript-845204).

acceptance_criteria.title: Nationality is asked and required only of employees living in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has entered the country of their home address as it applies on the first working day (step 2 'Home address')
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches step 3 'Nationality and C permit'
acceptance_criteria.then: the nationality is asked and required if the country of residence is Switzerland; it is not asked of employees living abroad, who are subject to source tax whatever their nationality (D-038). Nationality is recorded for HR to decide source tax liability and whether the permit reminder applies.

acceptance_criteria.title: Nationality answer values; Swiss citizenship counts as Swiss
acceptance_criteria.given: the nationality question is asked
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers it
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee chooses a country from the country list by English name, or 'stateless'. Anyone holding Swiss citizenship, also together with another nationality, answers Switzerland and counts as Swiss. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert: the country list with 'stateless' (D-050) and dual nationals counting as Swiss (D-008).

acceptance_criteria.title: C permit is asked only of non-Swiss employees living in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Switzerland and has answered the nationality question
acceptance_criteria.when: the nationality is not Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.then: the question 'Do you hold a C permit (permanent residence)?' is asked and required, with the answers 'yes' or 'no'; it is not asked of Swiss nationals or of employees living abroad. No other permit type is asked (assumption D-005, to be verified by a domain expert). The answer is recorded for HR to decide source tax liability.

stories.title: Ask the spouse's nationality, C permit and residence only when they can exempt the employee
stories.i_want: to be asked about my spouse's or registered partner's nationality, C permit and residence only when the answer can change whether I am subject to source tax
stories.so_that: the spouse exemption can be checked without collecting spouse data that no party needs (data minimisation)
stories.priority_reason: HR states the spouse exemption changes who has to pay source tax at all (F-hr_transcript-b90bd9); without these answers liability is wrong for cases like Tomás.

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse's nationality is asked only when the spouse exemption could apply
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Switzerland, is not Swiss and has answered 'no' to holding a C permit
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee gives the civil status Married or Registered partnership in step 4 'Civil status and spouse'
acceptance_criteria.then: the spouse's or registered partner's nationality is asked and required (country list by English name, or 'stateless'; a spouse with Swiss citizenship answers Switzerland). It is not asked for any other civil status, nor of employees who live abroad, are Swiss or hold a C permit, because the answer cannot change their source tax liability. Assumptions - to be verified by a domain expert: registered partnership counts as married and separated as single for source tax (D-003); asking only when the employee would otherwise be subject is inferred (F-hr_transcript-54d011).

examples.name: Married Swiss national living in Switzerland

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse's C permit is asked only for a non-Swiss spouse
acceptance_criteria.given: the spouse's nationality has been asked
acceptance_criteria.when: the spouse's nationality is not Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.then: the question whether the spouse or registered partner holds a C permit is asked and required, with the answers 'yes' or 'no'; for a Swiss spouse it is not asked. No other permit type of the spouse is asked (assumption D-005, to be verified by a domain expert).

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse's residence is asked only for a Swiss or C-permit spouse
acceptance_criteria.given: the spouse's nationality has been asked
acceptance_criteria.when: the spouse is Swiss or holds a C permit
acceptance_criteria.then: the question 'Does your spouse live in Switzerland?' is asked and required, with the answers 'yes' or 'no'; it is not asked when the spouse is neither Swiss nor a C-permit holder, because the exemption cannot apply. 'Here' in HR's wording is read as Switzerland. Assumptions - to be verified by a domain expert: D-043 and the yes/no form of the question (D-050).

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse answers that no longer apply are not kept
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has answered spouse questions and then changes an earlier answer (for example civil status to Single, or C permit to 'yes') so that they no longer apply
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee submits the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: the spouse answers that no longer apply are discarded and not recorded; before submission they are kept, so going back and forth loses no input.

stories.title: Decide whether the employee is subject to source tax
stories.i_want: Lonio to decide from the employee's answers whether they are subject to source tax, following HR's consolidated rule
stories.so_that: every employee who must pay source tax gets a tariff code and nobody who is exempt is charged
stories.priority_reason: Liability decides whether a tariff code is needed at all; HR corrected its own rule twice in the interview, showing the risk of errors (F-hr_transcript-845204, F-hr_transcript-5af8d0).

acceptance_criteria.title: Employees living abroad are always subject
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's home address on the first working day is outside Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio decides source tax liability
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is subject to source tax whatever their nationality or civil status; even a Swiss citizen living abroad is subject.

acceptance_criteria.title: Swiss nationals and C-permit holders living in Switzerland are not subject
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: the nationality is Switzerland (also as one of several nationalities), or the employee is not Swiss and holds a C permit
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is not subject to source tax, whatever their civil status. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert: anyone with Swiss citizenship counts as Swiss (D-008).

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse exemption for married employees and registered partners
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Switzerland, is not Swiss, has no C permit and is Married or in a Registered partnership
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio decides source tax liability
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is not subject if the spouse or registered partner is Swiss or holds a C permit and lives in Switzerland; otherwise the employee is subject. Assumptions - to be verified by a domain expert: registered partnership counts as married (D-003) and 'here' means Switzerland (D-043).

acceptance_criteria.title: No spouse exemption for single, divorced, widowed or separated employees
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Switzerland, is not Swiss and has no C permit
acceptance_criteria.when: the civil status is Single, Divorced, Widowed or Separated
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is subject to source tax; separated counts as single, so there is no spouse exemption. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert: D-003.

acceptance_criteria.title: Liability is always derived from the latest answers
acceptance_criteria.given: the questionnaire has been submitted and HR later changes an answer the decision depends on (for example the country of residence after a move, or the civil status after a marriage)
acceptance_criteria.when: the liability is derived again
acceptance_criteria.then: it follows the latest answers. If the change makes questions apply that were never asked (for example the spouse questions after a marriage), the result shows 'incomplete - HR must complete' until HR enters the missing answers; answers that no longer apply are discarded. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert: D-048. How HR makes the change is specified in the later HR-side spec (D-034).

stories.title: Derive the calculator's residence from the home address country
stories.i_want: Lonio to group the employee's country of residence the way the Zurich calculator does (Switzerland, Germany, Liechtenstein or other country) without asking a separate question
stories.so_that: the tariff code follows the calculator's residence logic and the employee is not asked their residence twice
stories.priority_reason: Lonio now computes the tariff code instead of HR (D-001); the residence group decides whether cross-border questions apply or the base tariff is used.

acceptance_criteria.title: Residence group follows the home address country
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has given the country of their home address as it applies on the first working day
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the residence for source tax
acceptance_criteria.then: Switzerland gives 'Switzerland', Germany gives 'Germany', Liechtenstein gives 'Liechtenstein' and any other country gives 'Other country'. Switzerland and other country lead to the base tariff without further residence questions. Assumption - to be verified by a domain expert: the residence that counts is the one on the first working day (D-041).

sections.title: Source tax: residence abroad and cross-border questions
sections.purpose: Group the country of residence as the calculator does. Ask Liechtenstein and Germany residents the cross-border questions (daily return, non-return days, certificate of residence) and derive whether the employee is in principle not liable to source tax (Liechtenstein) or the cross-border tariff applies (Germany).

stories.title: Derive the calculator's residence answers from the home address and ask cross-border questions only of Germany and Liechtenstein residents
stories.i_want: Lonio to group the employee's country of residence the way the Zurich calculator does (Switzerland, Germany, Liechtenstein or other country), without asking it again, and to ask the cross-border commuting questions only of employees living in Germany or Liechtenstein
stories.so_that: the tariff code can be computed by following the calculator's logic from the home address the employee already gave, and no employee is asked cross-border questions that no party needs for them
stories.priority_reason: Lonio computes the full tariff code instead of HR using the calculator (D-001); without the residence grouping no tariff code can be computed for any employee subject to source tax.

acceptance_criteria.title: Residence is grouped as in the calculator from the country of the home address
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has entered the country of their home address in step 2 'Home address', as it applies on their first working day (assumption D-041, to be verified by a domain expert)
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio determines the residence for source tax
acceptance_criteria.then: the residence is 'Switzerland' when the country is Switzerland, 'Germany' when it is Germany, 'Liechtenstein' when it is Liechtenstein, and 'Other country' for any other country; the employee is not asked a separate question about their main residence or country of residence for source tax

acceptance_criteria.title: Switzerland and other countries get no cross-border questions
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Switzerland or in a country other than Germany and Liechtenstein
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee goes through the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: step 5 'Cross-border commuting' is not shown and no question on daily return, non-return days, reasonableness of daily return or certificate of residence is asked; for source tax the base tariff applies without further residence questions, as in the calculator

acceptance_criteria.title: Germany and Liechtenstein residents get step 5 'Cross-border commuting'
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Germany or Liechtenstein (and is therefore subject to source tax, as every employee living abroad is)
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee has completed step 4 'Civil status and spouse'
acceptance_criteria.then: step 5 'Cross-border commuting' is shown before step 6 'Source tax details'; a Germany resident is asked the Germany questions starting with daily return to Germany, a Liechtenstein resident the Liechtenstein questions starting with daily return to Liechtenstein, and never the questions of the other country (step order is assumption D-047, to be verified by a domain expert)

examples.name: Calculator: Germany shows the daily return question (zh_source_tax_calculator/F-31d762)
Calculator: Liechtenstein shows the daily return question (zh_source_tax_calculator/F-e22d17)

acceptance_criteria.title: Cross-border answers that no longer apply are not kept
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee answered cross-border questions and then changes their home address country so that those questions no longer apply (for example from Germany to Switzerland)
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee submits the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: the cross-border answers that no longer apply are discarded and not recorded; before submission they are kept, so changing the country back restores them; after submission any change of the country is made by HR, and the residence grouping and every result of this section are derived again from the latest answers (D-036, D-037); if an HR change makes cross-border questions apply that were never asked, the tariff code shows 'incomplete - HR must complete' until HR enters the missing answers (assumption D-048, to be verified by a domain expert)

stories.title: Germany: daily return and certificate of residence
stories.i_want: an employee living in Germany to be asked whether they expect to return daily to their main residence in Germany and, if so, whether they have a certificate of residence for HR
stories.so_that: Lonio can decide, as the calculator does, whether the cross-border tariff applies and HR knows when a certificate is still expected
stories.priority_reason: The answer changes the tariff letter (e.g. C1Y becomes N1Y in the calculator); without it Lonio cannot compute the tariff code it now owns (D-001).

acceptance_criteria.title: Daily return to Germany is asked of every Germany resident
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's home address is in Germany
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches step 5 'Cross-border commuting'
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked whether they expect to return daily to their main residence in Germany, answering 'yes' or 'no'; the answer is required and is recorded for source tax; it is a statement of what the employee expects, no document is asked; employees living in any other country are not asked

acceptance_criteria.title: Certificate of residence is asked only with daily return
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Germany
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee answers that they return daily
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked whether they have a certificate of residence for HR, answering 'yes', 'no' or 'not yet'; the answer is required and is recorded for source tax and for HR, so HR knows a certificate is still expected; the certificate itself goes to HR outside Lonio and is not uploaded; when the employee does not return daily the question is not asked

acceptance_criteria.title: Cross-border tariff with daily return depends on the certificate
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Germany and returns daily
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio decides whether the cross-border tariff applies
acceptance_criteria.then: with a certificate of residence the cross-border tariff applies; with 'no' or 'not yet' the normal tariff applies ('not yet' counts as 'no', D-035); the cross-border letters follow the calculator in full (A to L, B to M, C to N, H to P, G to Q; assumption D-051, to be verified by a domain expert); if the certificate is handed in later, HR changes the answer after submission and the tariff code is derived again (D-037)

acceptance_criteria.title: Only Germany residents can get the cross-border tariff
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee does not live in Germany
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio decides whether the cross-border tariff applies

flow.intro: The questionnaire has eight steps in a fixed order. Only the questions that apply to this employee are shown, and a step where no question applies is skipped. The order follows dependency: the home address country decides who is asked for nationality and cross-border details. Civil status and spouse answers come before the source tax details. Liechtenstein cross-border questions come before the source tax details, because they decide whether those details are needed at all. Children come last, after the question of whether the employee has any. Answers are saved as the employee goes and can be resumed until submission. Going back and changing an earlier answer keeps the other answers until submission.

steps.title: About you
steps.asks: First name, last name, date of birth and first working day.

steps.title: Home address
steps.asks: Street, house number, postcode, town and country of the home address as on the first working day; the canton of residence only if the country is Switzerland.

steps.title: Nationality and C permit
steps.asks: Nationality; whether the employee holds a C permit only if not Swiss.
steps.shown_to: Employees living in Switzerland (skipped for employees living abroad)

steps.title: Civil status and spouse
steps.asks: Civil status. Date of birth of the spouse or registered partner if Married, Registered partnership or Separated. If the employee lives in Switzerland, is not Swiss, has no C permit and is married or in a registered partnership: the spouse's nationality, whether the spouse holds a C permit (only if the spouse is not Swiss), and whether the spouse lives in Switzerland (only if the spouse is Swiss or holds a C permit).
steps.shown_to: Everyone for civil status; the spouse questions only as described

steps.title: Cross-border commuting
steps.asks: Liechtenstein: daily return, and if not daily, more than 45 work-related non-return days. Germany: daily return; if daily, whether a certificate of residence has been handed in ('not yet' counts as no); if not daily, whether daily return is reasonable (less than 100 km) and, if reasonable, more than 60 work-related non-return days.
steps.shown_to: Employees living in Liechtenstein or Germany who are subject to source tax (skipped for everyone else)

steps.title: Source tax details
steps.asks: Denomination; whether the spouse or partner is gainfully employed (only if married or in a registered partnership); whether the employee has biological or adopted children.
steps.shown_to: Employees subject to source tax; for Liechtenstein residents only with more than 45 non-return days (skipped if there is in principle no source tax liability)

steps.title: Children
steps.asks: One block per child: minor or adult in first education; whether the child lives in the same household; then, depending on the answers, custody, common household with the other parent, shared custody, parental care, alternating custody, who contributes more financially, and whether more than 50% of maintenance is provided.
steps.shown_to: Employees subject to source tax who have children (skipped otherwise)

steps.title: Permit reminder, summary and submission
steps.asks: Nothing new is asked. The employee sees a reminder to bring their permit on the first working day, reviews a summary of the answers and submits with one confirmation.
steps.shown_to: Everyone; the permit reminder only to non-Swiss employees living in Switzerland and to all employees living abroad

flow.closing: After submission the questionnaire is read-only for the employee. Answers that no longer apply are discarded on submission. Any later change is made by HR, and all derived results are derived again from the latest answers.
